entities.label: AgentObligationBinding
entities.rationale: An agent-obligation binding is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in an agent (bearer) and is externally grounded in a normative/legal structure that prescribes the obligation. It is not internally grounded (which would make it a Disposition) but rather socially and institutionally conferred — paradigmatically a Role in BFO. The binding relationship between an agent and an obligation is best captured as a Role class because it represents the normative position the agent occupies relative to the obligation, contingent on the legal or social context. It relates closely to the existing working:LegalObligation (which is itself typed as BFO_0000023), but AgentObligationBinding is the class of role-instances that tie a specific agent to a specific obligatory content. Alternatively, one might argue it is a Disposition (BFO_0000016) if the binding is read as an internal capacity to be bound; see open_questions.

relations.rationale: AgentObligationBinding is a subclass of Role (BFO_0000023) because it is an externally grounded specifically dependent continuant inhering in an agent-bearer, conferred by a normative system.

AgentObligationBinding is a specialization of LegalObligation: it is specifically the binding of a legal obligation to a particular agent, rather than the general class of legal obligations. This subclass relation anchors it in the existing hierarchy.

open_questions: Is 'agent-obligation binding' intended to denote the normative tie between a specific agent and a specific obligation (favoring Role, BFO_0000023, externally grounded), or the internal susceptibility/capacity of an agent to be bound by obligations (favoring Disposition, BFO_0000016, internally grounded)?

Should AgentObligationBinding be a subclass of the existing working:LegalObligation (as proposed), or should it be a sibling class under BFO_0000023 representing a distinct relational structure between agents and obligations?

Is this meant to represent a class of such bindings in general, or a specific binding individual (e.g., a particular agent bound to a particular rule)? If the latter, it should be typed as an individual rather than a class.

Does 'agent' here refer exclusively to human legal persons, or also to corporate/institutional agents? This affects whether the bearer constraint on the inhering Role should be restricted to persons or extended to legal institutions.
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'agent-obligation binding' denotes the relationship by which a normative obligation attaches to or inheres in a specific agent. In BFO 2020, this is most naturally classified as a Role (BFO_0000023), a species of Realizable Entity under Specifically Dependent Continuant: it inheres in the agent as bearer, but its existence and character are externally grounded in the legal or normative system that imposes the obligation — not in any intrinsic property of the agent. This distinguishes it from a Disposition (BFO_0000016), which would be internally grounded. The proposed class AgentObligationBinding is placed as a subclass of BFO_0000023 and, more specifically, as a subclass of the existing working:LegalObligation, which is already typed as a Role. Key open questions remain about whether the term names a class or individual, and whether the grounding is truly external (Role) or internal (Disposition), which the user should clarify before committing the triple to the graph.
